semantic_nodes.canonical_text: 3-38 LOGIQ e – Basic Service Manual 5937432-1EN Rev. 4
This section describes how to install and configure the peripherals validated for the LOGIQ e.
About the operation check-out of peripherals, See 'Peripheral Checks' on page 4-56 for more information.
This section describes the materials furnished with the Peripherals and with the system.
Retain the original carton and packing materials in case transport is needed in the future.
Table 3-13: Materials furnished with B/W Printer
Table 3-14: Materials furnished with Color USB Printer
3-40 LOGIQ e – Basic Service Manual 5937432-1EN Rev. 4
Table 3-16: Materials furnished with the Wireless LAN
Table 3-17: Materials furnished with the Footswitch
Table 3-18: Materials furnished with the Barcode Scanner
Place the device in a suitable place.
Connect power cord and USB Cable on the Printer.
Figure 3-19. Color Printer USB cable and Power Cord connect
Connect the power cord to the outlet on the wall, then turn on the printer.
3-42 LOGIQ e – Basic Service Manual 5937432-1EN Rev. 4
Connect USB cable to LOGIQ e USB port.
Setting up Color printer for Printing Report
Connect the color printer to the USB port of the system.
Power on the printer and the system.
After the system completes booting up, enter Utility -> System -> Peripherals, select UP-D25MD for Standard Printer.
Assigning Printer Key to the Printer
Example below assign P2 on the control panel to Color Printer UP-D25MD.
Select Connectivity -> Service, select Standard Print in the Service list.
Select Connectivity -> Button, select Print2 in Print Button list, then select the original setting in Printflow View field and select "<<".
Select Standard Print, then press ">>" to add the standard printer to the Printflow View.
3-44 LOGIQ e – Basic Service Manual 5937432-1EN Rev. 4
NOTE: For SW R11.0.8 or before, please select 898 Printer Driver for Sony UP-D899MD. For system with software version outside the abovementioned scope, please skip this step.
Follow the below procedures to select the 898 Printer Driver:
When Printer is in 'READY' Mode, push the 'PUSH ENTER' button to enter the 'PRT.MENU' Mode.
Toggle the 'PUSH ENTER' button downwards two times to enter the 'DIGITAL' Mode and push the 'PUSH ENTER' button again to enter 'DRIVER' Mode.
Push the 'PUSH ENTER' button again and toggle the 'PUSH ENTER' button upwards or downwards to select the 898 printer driver.
3-46 LOGIQ e – Basic Service Manual 5937432-1EN Rev. 4
Place the device in a suitable place.
Connect the USB Cable on the DVD-RW.
Figure 3-28. Connect USB cable on DVD-RW
Connect USB cable to LOGIQ e USB port.
Do Not connect DVD-RW with the system while scanning.
3-48 LOGIQ e – Basic Service Manual 5937432-1EN Rev. 4
Connect the Wireless LAN Adapter to the USB port on the LOGIQ e system.
Figure 3-30. Connect Wireless LAN Adapter to the system
Enter Utility -> Connectivity -> TCP/IP and select Configuration to configure wireless network.
Config the wireless Lan setting with local IT person.
3-50 LOGIQ e – Basic Service Manual 5937432-1EN Rev. 4
A Wireless Network (WLAN) is available on the LOGIQ e. When the WLAN is active, an icon appears in the status bar to indicate whether the WLAN is installed or disconnected.
The Wireless LAN (WLAN) supports the following network protocols
Limited support for server certificate verification using pre-installed trusted root CAS
This wireless adapter supports the following network protocols:
3-52 LOGIQ e – Basic Service Manual 5937432-1EN Rev. 4
This wireless adapter supports the following network protocols:
This wireless adapter supports the following network protocols:
To connect the LOGIQ e to the WLAN,
Press Utility --> Connectivity --> TCP/IP --> Wireless Network --> Configuration.
The Wireless Network Configuration tool appears. Available Wireless Networks appear.
Highlight the wireless network you want to use.
Press Connect from the bottom of the Configuration tool. The Active Wireless LAN indicator appears on the display.
NOTE: If the WLAN fails to connect, review and/or recreate the
Wireless connection on the Security Tab.
3-54 LOGIQ e – Basic Service Manual 5937432-1EN Rev. 4
To add a WLAN profile (even for a network which is not yet available),
Press Utility--> Connectivity--> TCP/IP--> Wireless Network--> Configuration -> Security. The Wireless Network Configuration tool appears. Available Wireless Networks appear.
Obtain and enter the correct information for each wireless network setting.
Enter a Network Name (SSID), then press OK. A new window appears so you can enter the settings for this network.
On the connection page, check the appropriate box based on how you want the LOGIQ e to connect to this network.

The LOGIQ e attempts to connect to available wireless networks based on the options you enable. If multiple networks are available, connection attempts begin with the network appearing topmost on the list.
LOGIQ e – Basic Service Manual 3-55 5937432-1EN Rev. 4
Select the Security Type from the available options.
NOTE: Dialog boxes vary, depending on the Security Type selected.
3-56 LOGIQ e – Basic Service Manual 5937432-1EN Rev. 4
Select the Encryption Type from the available options.
For Personal networks, enter the Network key.
For Enterprise network, choose the network authentication method and press Settings.

Detailed settings for Enterprise networks are complex and must be correct for the connection to succeed. Ensure you have all the required information/settings and work with your site's IT Network Administrator as needed.
NOTE: Creditials must be entered at this time. The LOGIQ e does not support automatic prompting for user credentials.
For Microsoft PEAP networks, press Advanced and enter User authentication credentials (username and password).
For Cisco networks, enter user credentials in the PEAP Properties dialog after pressing the Settings button.
NOTE: IMPORTANT: User credentials are not validated until you attempt to connect to the network.

When you have correctly entered all required settings, press OK in the Wireless Network Properties dialog. Your settings will be validated and you may be prompted about certain settings which are not recommended or supported.
Examples: "Automatic connection to unencrypted networks is not recommended. Reminder to enter user credentials for Enterprise networks."
If changes are necessary, press Customize. Make corrections, then press OK. Settings will be validated again.
After you have filled in all the required information, press OK. To cancel adding this profile, press Cancel .
3-58 LOGIQ e – Basic Service Manual 5937432-1EN Rev. 4
To remove a WLAN profile (even for a network which is not available),
Press Utility--> Connectivity--> TCP/IP--> Wireless Network--> Security. The Wireless Network Configuration tool appears. Available Wireless Networks appear.
To customize an existing WLAN profile,
Press Utility--> Connectivity--> TCP/IP--> Wireless Network--> Configuration. The Wireless Network Configuration tool appears. Available Wireless Networks appear.
Network Authentication (Open, Shared Key, WPA PSK, or WPA2 PSK).
After you have filled in all the required information, press OK. To cancel adding this profile, press Cancel .
LOGIQ e – Basic Service Manual 3-59 5937432-1EN Rev. 4
Refreshes the list of available Wireless Networks. To refresh the Wireless Network,
Press Utility--> Connectivity--> TCP/IP--> Wireless Network--> Configuration. The Wireless Network Configuration tool appears. Available Wireless Networks appear.
Highlight the wireless network you want to refresh.
Press Refresh from the bottom of the Configuration tool.

When you make a WLAN non-preferable, you disconnect the network from the system and delete all connection settings from the system. Afterwards, the system WILL NOT try to reconnect to this WLAN automatically. And if you want to reconnect, you will need to re-add this WLAN.
Press Utility--> Connectivity--> TCP/IP--> Wireless Network--> Configuration. The Wireless Network Configuration tool appears. Available Wireless Networks appear.
Highlight the wireless network you want to set as non-preferred.

Press Make Non-Preferable from the bottom of the Configuration tool. You wil receive the following message to confirm this decision: "Are you sure you wish to make network _______ non-preferable? Network will be disconnected and system will not reconnect to this network automatically. Network connection settings will be deleted from the system."
3-60 LOGIQ e – Basic Service Manual 5937432-1EN Rev. 4
If there are wireless network communication problems, you can monitor the wireless network events.
Press Utility--> Connectivity--> TCP/IP--> Wireless Network--> Configuration. The Wireless Network Configuration tool appears. Available Wireless Networks appear.

Running diagnostics is good if you think the adapter might be bad. Diagnostics also tell you if the connection is behaving properly. Sometimes the scanner connects by accident to another internal device which uses the TCP/IP protocol. The diagnostics would show if there are errors when performing the full two-way communication. For example, if the IP address starts with 197 or 169 (loopback addresses), then something is wrong.
Press Utility--> Connectivity--> TCP/IP--> Wireless Network--> Configuration. The Wireless Network Configuration tool appears. Available Wireless Networks appear.
3-62 LOGIQ e – Basic Service Manual 5937432-1EN Rev. 4
Occasionally you may need to repair a WLAN that has lost its connection to the LOGIQ e. To repair the Wireless Network,
Press Utility--> Connectivity--> TCP/IP--> Wireless Network--> Configuration. The Wireless Network Configuration tool appears. Available Wireless Networks appear.
NOTE: DO NOT cancel the Repair operation after you have selected to repair the Wireless LAN connection.
If the WLAN is functioning properly, the following message appears. Confirm your decision to repair (Yes), or cancel (No).

The available WLAN channels show availability of wireless connect points that the scanner can talk to. Each channel supports a finite number of users and has limited signal strength. This may effect the ability to connect, the throughput and the connection dropping out.
To check the available WLAN channels,
Press Utility--> Connectivity--> TCP/IP--> Wireless Network--> Configuration. The Wireless Network Configuration tool appears. Available Wireless Networks appear.
3-64 LOGIQ e – Basic Service Manual 5937432-1EN Rev. 4
To disconnect from the Wireless Network,
Press Utility--> Connectivity--> TCP/IP--> Wireless Network--> Configuration. The Wireless Network Configuration tool appears.
Select the WLAN you are connected to.
To view the WLAN Online Help, press Help .
Connect the Footswitch to the USB port on the LOGIQ e system.
Figure 3-45. Connect Footswitch to the system
3-66 LOGIQ e – Basic Service Manual 5937432-1EN Rev. 4

Footswitch supports these configurations: No Function, Rec/ Pause, Freeze, Next Heartcycle, Prev Heartcycle, Print 1, Print 2, Print 3, Print 4, Update, Next Step (Scan Assistant), Previous Step (Scan Assistant), Scan Assistant Pause/Resume or Mark Cine. The default setting is No Function.
Enter Utility -> Application -> Settings to configure the Footswitch functions.
Connect the Barcode Scanner to the USB port on the LOGIQ e system.
Figure 3-47. Connect Barcode Scanner to the system
NOTE: After the Barcode Scanner is connected to the LOGIQ e Cart, the cable of the Barcode Scanner can be hung in the cable hook.
3-68 LOGIQ e – Basic Service Manual 5937432-1EN Rev. 4
The barcode scanner needs to be set up before the first use.
To set up the barcode scanner, follow the steps below:
Power on the system. Connect barcode scanner to the system.

Firstly, scan the Remove Custom Defaults barcode (1). Secondly, scan the Activate Defaults barcode (2). Thirdly, scan the To enable 1900 PID code(3). Finally, scan the USB Serial barcode (4). The Barcode scanner is ready for use.
LOGIQ e – Basic Service Manual 3-69 5937432-1EN Rev. 4
NOTE: Only the printed barcodes on the paper can be scanned. If you do not have the printed version, be sure to print them to the paper first and scan them on the paper.
3-70 LOGIQ e – Basic Service Manual 5937432-1EN Rev. 4
LOGIQ e – Basic Service Manual 3-71 5937432-1EN Rev. 4
Connect the ECG to the USB port on the system (For ECG installation on LOGIQ e Cart, please refer to See 'Mounting Procedure of ECG' on page 11-21 for more information.).
Wait 5 seconds for ECG function start automatically.
ECG is intended to disclose either normal condition or patterns of arrhythmia, or features of prognostic value in the following cases:
Populations of patients at an age or period in which a routine baseline evaluation of ECG characteristics is desired.
3-72 LOGIQ e – Basic Service Manual 5937432-1EN Rev. 4

The ECG traces quality depends very much on the stability and conductivity of the electrodes during the test, especially during high stages when the patient movements can cause artifacts. Here are some basic rules to ensure good electrical contact:
Shave hair at the electrode contact points.
Use a special shirt that attached the electrodes and lead wires to the body.
Use high quality liquid gel electrodes.
Make sure that the lead wires do not swing.

Detachable 3 leads each 100cm with clip connectors on the patient end designed for use with disposable ECG electrodes. Furthermore, equip 3 repeatable limbs electrode clamps which can connect with clip connector. Limbs electrodes are white, red and green (AHA\IEC).
LOGIQ e – Basic Service Manual 3-73 5937432-1EN Rev. 4
3-74 LOGIQ e – Basic Service Manual 5937432-1EN Rev. 4
